    C = np.array(mat)
    K = C.shape[0]
    # macro F1 from column-stochastic C: precision_k = C[k,k]/sum(C[:,k]), recall not directly available
    # Actually C is column-stochastic: C[j,k] = P(A*=j|A=k). So:
    # precision for class k = C[k,k] / sum(C[k,:])  (predicted k and truly k / all predicted k)
    # recall for class k = C[k,k] / sum(C[:,k]) = C[k,k] (column sums to 1)
    # But we need counts not probabilities. With uniform p_A:
    # Let p_A be uniform for simplicity or use actual marginals
    p_A = np.ones(K) / K  # assume uniform for now
    
    # P(predicted=j) = sum_k C[j,k] * p_A[k]
    p_pred = C @ p_A
    
    # precision_k = C[k,k] * p_A[k] / p_pred[k]
    # recall_k = C[k,k] (since columns sum to 1)
    f1_per_class = []
    for k in range(K):
        prec = C[k,k] * p_A[k] / p_pred[k] if p_pred[k] > 0 else 0
        rec = C[k,k]
        if prec + rec > 0:
            f1_per_class.append(2 * prec * rec / (prec + rec))
        else:

    macro_f1 = np.mean(f1_per_class)
